name: Plaza Principal (Town Center)
tagline: Samaipata's walkable heart, market, cafes, and daily life
description: The central plaza and surrounding blocks hold the market, most restaurants, expat-run cafes, guesthouses, and the trufi stop for Santa Cruz. Everything a nomad needs day to day is within a 10-minute walk, making this the default base for short stays or anyone without a vehicle.
bestFor: first-time visitors and short-term nomads wanting walkability
pros: easy transport connections to Santa Cruz
cons: fewer garden or quiet outdoor spaces

name: Camino a El Fuerte
tagline: The road toward the ruins, quieter guesthouses and valley views
description: Heading east out of town toward El Fuerte de Samaipata, the road passes scattered guesthouses, small farms, and lodgings with valley and mountain views. It's a short drive or a longer walk from the plaza, popular with visitors who want quiet mornings and easy access to the archaeological site.
bestFor: travelers prioritizing the El Fuerte site and nature over nightlife
pros: cooler air away from town center
cons: need transport into town for daily errands

name: Las Cuevas / outskirts residential
tagline: Where longer-term expats and residents settle, gardens and houses
description: The residential fringe on the edges of Samaipata, including areas locals call Las Cuevas, hosts rental houses with gardens, popular with longer-term expats and families. It trades some walkability for space, quiet, and lower rents, with a short trufi or motorbike ride into the plaza for supplies and cafes.
bestFor: longer-term nomads wanting more space and quiet
pros: more affordable rentals with outdoor space
cons: need a bike or vehicle for daily trips into town

name: Valle de Bermejo
tagline: A nearby valley toward Amboró, waterfalls and cloud forest access
description: The Bermejo valley area, a short drive from Samaipata toward the Amboró National Park side, is where the cloud forest and giant tree ferns become dramatic. A handful of eco-lodges and rural homestays sit here, appealing to nature-focused visitors willing to trade town convenience for direct access to trails and waterfalls.
bestFor: nature lovers and hikers wanting an Amboró-adjacent base
pros: closest access to Amboró trails and waterfalls
cons: unpaved roads, rough or impassable after heavy rain
